title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter V, 'Algèbre des figures', 1986. Grothendieck studies a family 𝔉 of subsets ('figures') of a set L. Each A in 𝔉 has an 'open part' A° = A minus the union of the members of 𝔉 strictly contained in A. On the previous page, 𝔉 is called pre-admissible when conditions 1°–3° hold. Roughly, these say the A° partition |𝔉| = ∪𝔉, and each A is the union of the B° with B ⊂ A. The family is admissible if in addition A° ≠ ∅ for every A in 𝔉 (top line of this page).

Proposition 2 (this page). Giving an admissible family 𝔉 of subsets of L is the same as giving three things:
(a) a poset I, which is a faithful copy of (𝔉, ⊂);
(b) a subset S ⊂ L, namely S = |𝔉|;
(c) a surjection φ: S → I, sending x to the unique A(x) with x in A(x)°.

Recovering 𝔉 from (I, S, φ):
- Give I its Alexandrov topology. The closed sets are the down-sets (arbitrary unions of the I_{≤i}); the open sets are the up-sets (unions of the I_{≥i}).
- Give S the inverse-image topology, which is the topology of the preorder pulled back along φ.
- Then 𝔉 = { closure of φ^{-1}(i) = φ^{-1}(I_{≤i}) }, for i in I, and this indexation is injective.

Consequences:
- The strata are A_i° = φ^{-1}(i).
- The closed subsets of S correspond bijectively, via φ, to the closed (down-closed) subsets J of I. For such J, A_J = ∪_{i∈J} A_i = ⊔_{i∈J} A_i°, a disjoint union of nonempty parts.
- The page breaks off at 'De même, les parties ouvertes sont exactement de la forme'. The next page continues: open sets are φ^{-1}(J) for J an up-set; locally closed sets are φ^{-1}(J) for J convex; the Boolean algebra generated by 𝔉 consists of the φ-saturated sets, the A° being its atoms when 𝔉 is finite ('Φ-constructible' parts).

Margin: from a pre-admissible 𝔉 one obtains an admissible 𝔉' = {A ∈ 𝔉 : A° ≠ ∅}, defining the same partition, with I' = 𝔉' a subposet of I.

In modern terms: a 'stratification' of a set S is exactly a map to a poset. Equivalently, it is a continuous map to that poset with its Alexandrov topology, under which closures of strata are preimages of principal down-sets. This is the frontier condition built in.

Purpose: to lay set-theoretic foundations for an 'algebra of figures', meaning constructible sets and stratifications with their Boolean/valuation calculus, presumably towards Euler-characteristic-type invariants or tame-topology dévissage.
errors: No real error. One step is implicit: for the converse to work, the inclusion between φ^{-1}(I_{≤j}) and φ^{-1}(I_{≤i}) must reflect the order j ≤ i. This uses surjectivity of φ; it gives injectivity of the indexation and A_i° = φ^{-1}(i) ≠ ∅. The page leaves this implicit.
The equality 'closure of φ^{-1}(i) = φ^{-1}(closure of {i})' relies on S carrying the inverse-image (initial) topology. That is stated, but closure does not commute with preimage in general.
The parenthetical 'les ouverts les réunions quelc. d'ens. I_{≥i}' is correct for the Alexandrov topology in which the down-sets are the closed sets.

ideas.what: Admissible family of subsets (closed strata with nonempty open parts A°) is equivalent to a poset I plus a surjection φ: S → I; closed strata are φ^{-1}(I_{≤i})
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified set/space: a stratification as a (continuous) map to a poset with the Alexandrov topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in stratification theory. Formalized as definition by Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A.5, ~2009–2017); also Treumann, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2010s).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses stratified structures and 'dévissage' but, to my knowledge, not this explicit poset formulation

ideas.what: Alexandrov topology on a poset: closed = down-sets, open = up-sets; inverse-image topology on S
ideas.where_published: Specialization order of points appears in EGA I for schemes

ideas.what: Closed (resp. open, locally closed) unions of strata correspond to down-sets (resp. up-sets, convex sets) of I, with A_J a disjoint union of open strata
ideas.modern_name: Closed/open/locally closed unions of strata; constructible sets relative to a stratification

ideas.what: Passing from pre-admissible to admissible by discarding the A with A° empty

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck explicitly encodes a stratification as a surjection onto a poset carrying the Alexandrov topology (down-sets closed), with closed strata = φ^{-1}(I_{≤i}). This is precisely the convention later adopted as the foundational definition of 'P-stratified space' in Lurie's Higher Algebra A.5 and in exit-path/constructible-sheaf theory. It is an early, independent instance of that formalism, embedded in a project on an 'algebra of figures'.
missed.quote: Se donner une famille admissible 𝔉 de parties, revient ... à se donner a) Un ens. ordonné I ... b) Une partie S de L ... c) Une application surjective φ : S → I
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck's tame-topology/dévissage program using the now-standard poset-stratification formalism decades before its codification. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary and folklore. The only point of interest is the clean, modern-looking formulation of stratifications as maps to Alexandrov posets in an unpublished 1986 text, anticipating later conventions.
